species.name: Marandu grass
species.description: A pasture grass brought to Brazil from Africa. It forms dense clumps and can spread outside planted areas.
species.fireNote: Dry grass blades can form a continuous layer of fine fuel.
species.identification: Look for a dense tussock with long linear leaves and a branched seed head.

sources.title: Plants of the World Online: Urochloa brizantha
Fire cues and germination of invasive and native grasses in the Cerrado

species.name: Guinea grass
species.description: A tall grass brought from Africa for pasture. It can spread into disturbed areas and form dense clumps.
species.fireNote: Dead blades can remain in the clump and burn when dry.
species.identification: Look for tall clumps with long leaves and an open branching seed head.

species.name: Cecropia tree
species.description: A native tree that often grows in openings. Its broad leaves have deep lobes.
species.fireNote: Fallen leaves can burn after they dry.
species.identification: Look for large palmately lobed leaves and ring scars around the stem.

sources.title: Plants of the World Online: Cecropia obtusa
Synchronization of growth, branching and flowering processes in Cecropia obtusa

species.name: Phenakospermum
species.description: A large native herb with broad upright leaves. It often grows in disturbed forest.
species.fireNote: Old leaves add to the material on the forest floor.
species.identification: Look for very large upright leaves on long stalks and broad overlapping bases.

species.name: Bacaba palm
species.description: A native palm with a single trunk. People use its dark fruits for food.
species.fireNote: Check the fallen fronds as well as the living leaves.
species.identification: Look for one smooth trunk and a crown of long pinnate fronds.

sources.title: Plants of the World Online: Oenocarpus bacaba
Morphology and germination development of Oenocarpus bacaba

species.name: River fern
species.description: A native fern with long divided fronds. It grows on the ground and sometimes on other plants.
species.fireNote: A green fern can have dry material beneath it.
species.identification: Look for a dense tuft of narrow fronds with many small pinnae.
